newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Go-slow disrupts Zimbabwe air services.
newsitem.headline: Go-slow disrupts Zimbabwe air services.

text.p: A go-slow action by aircraft technicians at Zimbabwe's state-owned airline has disrupted some domestic and international flights, an Air Zimbabwe official said on Friday.
"Some flights have had to be cancelled or rescheduled as a result of this action (which began on Wednesday)," he told reporters.
Air Zimbabwe was also forced to hire a 118-seater Boeing 727 from a South African company to keep four planes running as its other four were grounded by the go-slow, he said.
"They (technicians) are working on them, but it's a slow process. But it looks like we will get some solution today," he said of talks to end the go-slow.

The technicians -- who were awarded a 27 percent salary rise two months ago -- are demanding another 15 percent increase on the grounds that their wages are still low for workers classified as critical by the government.
Thousands of Zimbabwean civil servants, mostly doctors and nurses, have been on strike since Monday, also for higher wages.
President Robert Mugabe's government has opened talks with the civil servants over their demands.
